page: Amazon Web Services c5n.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server instance designed for high-throughput networking and compute-intensive workloads. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8124M processor built on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 36 physical cores and 72 vCPUs at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR4 system memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 2.67 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

The hardware configuration delivers strong multi-core performance and memory bandwidth. In benchmark testing, the multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and PassMark CPU scores rank in the top 25%, demonstrating the efficiency of its 72 vCPUs under parallel workloads. Memory read-only bandwidth for both small and large blocks, along with large-block write operations, also registers in the top 25%. Conversely, single-core performance metrics, such as single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core scores, fall within the average range. LLM text generation speeds are poor, though prompt processing speeds remain average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c5n.metal offers high resource density for parallel processing and network-heavy operations without the overhead of a hypervisor. The inclusion of a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth makes it highly suitable for distributed applications, clustered databases, and high-performance computing nodes. However, the lack of local storage requires external storage provisioning, which may introduce latency tradeoffs depending on the storage architecture.

This server is best suited for network-bound and compute-heavy workloads. These include high-performance web serving, database operations, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and scientific simulations that leverage its AVX-512 instruction support.
